meta.name: Rainbow Childrens Medicare Ltd
meta.about: Rainbow Children's Medicare Limited operates a multi-specialty pediatric, obstetrics, and gynecology hospital chain in India. The company offers a wide range of services such as newborn and pediatric intensive care, pediatric multi-specialty services, pediatric quaternary care, obstetrics, and gynecology. [1] It is country’s largest pediatric hospital chain with 16 hospitals spread across 6 cities.[2]
meta.keyPoints: Business Overview:[1] The company operates 24 hospitals and 5 clinics across 9 cities, with a total bed capacity of 2,565. It specializes in pediatric healthcare under "Rainbow Children's Hospital" and women's healthcare under "Birthright by Rainbow."
pros: Company's median sales growth is 22.8% of last 10 years
cons: Stock is trading at 7.58 times its book value

company.annualKpiNote: opBedsAvg = weighted-average operational beds the company uses for occupancy (year-end operational beds: 1,523 at Mar-25, 1,806 at Mar-26). Occupancy = occupied bed days ÷ (weighted operational beds × days); ARPOB = total operating revenue ÷ occupied bed days (so it includes OP and pharmacy revenue); ALOS = occupied bed days ÷ IP discharges. Revenue = occupancy × beds × 365 × ARPOB reconciles to reported revenue within 0.3% in FY23-FY26.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Rainbow Children's Medicare (consolidated, ₹ crore). One reportable segment, so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and a post-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin (Screener basis: rent is not in EBITDA; lease interest sits in interest and right-of-use depreciation in depreciation; lease liabilities sit in borrowings, so the model's net cash is net of leases). The bed build (mature hospitals, new hospitals, pipeline) sits in `businessLines`; the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue. Profit is attributable to owners (RAINBOW.patch.js); the tax line carries the 24% minorities in the acquired hospitals. Valued on EV/EBITDA, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the bed build below (beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB, plus pipeline hospitals). FY27 +22%: Q1 +33% (organic ~24%; acquisitions ₹38 cr), Q2 guided 'above 20%', the acquisition boost fades from Q3 (Guwahati and Warangal were consolidated from Aug-25 and Jul-25) and the 2026 monsoon was late and deficient; management guides ~20% and 'cross ₹2,000 cr'. FY28 +21%, FY29 +20%: ARPOB +5-6% a year (management: ARPP 5-6%), occupancy of new hospitals rising from 34% toward the mid-40s, and the pipeline (Malad, Coimbatore, Gurugram, Pune) starting with low occupancy. Management's medium-term ambition is ~20% a year (double revenue in four years after FY27).

businessLines._why: Mature = the 1,202 operational beds that management classifies as mature from FY27 (Q1FY27: occupancy 45.0%, ARPOB ₹70,662). Full-year occupancy has run ~6-8pp above Q1 (FY25 50.5% vs 42.4%; FY26 46.3% vs 40.2%) and ARPOB ~2-5% below Q1, so FY27 mature = 50.5% and ₹67,500 (a normal-to-weak season after a late monsoon), then +1-1.5pp of occupancy and +5-6% ARPOB a year (still below the 56% mature occupancy of FY25). New = the 10 hospitals under five years old (Q1FY27: 660 operational of 885 capacity beds, occupancy 34.4%, ARPOB ₹59,133): operational beds rise as HRBR, Electronic City and Warangal fill (690 / 760 / 800 weighted), occupancy 38% / 43% / 46%, ARPOB ₹57,000 / 60,400 / 63,500. Pipeline revenue is GAM's estimate per hospital (beds × months open × ~25-45% occupancy × ₹45,000-85,000 ARPOB, by city), using the opening dates management gave on 31-Jul-2026; we assume slow ramps for the Gurugram hub and Pune.

assumptions._marginWhy: Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin (Screener basis): 33% FY24-25, 32.2% FY26, 28.7% in Q1FY27 (29.5% a year earlier). Management guides the pre-Ind AS margin back to 24-25% for FY27 (Q1FY27 23.0%; FY26 26.3%); rent is ~5pp of revenue (Ind AS impact ₹96 cr in FY26, ₹26 cr in Q1FY27), so 24.5-25% pre-Ind AS ≈ 29.7-30.2% post. FY28 30.5%: HRBR and Electronic City break even (12-18 months guided), offset by start-up losses at Malad, Coimbatore and Gurugram Sector 56. FY29 30.0%: the 325-bed Gurugram hub, Pune and Seegehalli open. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹25 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~5% of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex ₹380 / 460 / 480 cr plus new leases (right-of-use additions) ₹100 / 120 / 100 cr. Cash: maintenance ~₹45 cr a year; Gurugram ₹400-500 cr over two years (own land, own build); other projects at ₹65-70 lakh a bed (Coimbatore 130, Pune 150, Indore 100, Seegehalli 80, Malad fit-out); five-year plan ₹2,200 cr for 2,500 beds (~₹440 cr a year). FY26 capex ₹217 cr, Q1FY27 ₹56 cr. New leases are added because the model's net debt includes lease liabilities: right-of-use additions were ₹146 cr in FY26 (AR note 2.32), and Guntur, Malad, Indore and Seegehalli are leased. Engine workaround: a new lease adds an asset and a liability without cash, which the engine can only show as capex funded from net cash. The Nellore acquisition price is not disclosed and is left out.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹151 cr (incl. right-of-use depreciation ₹54 cr) = 6.6% of average gross block (₹2,294 cr); Q1FY27 ₹42 cr (₹169 cr annualised). 6.5% gives FY27E ≈ ₹181 cr with the new hospitals; the engine depreciates capex at once while projects sit in CWIP.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after lease liabilities, which is negative (₹583 cr of cash, deposits and investments less ₹891 cr of leases at Mar-26). Treasury income is built on gross cash in `otherIncome` instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 2.21). (1) Treasury income = yield × opening gross cash, deposits and mutual funds: FY26 ₹38.4 cr (bank interest ₹8.0 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹30.4 cr) on ~₹645 cr average funds = ~6.0%; company cash & investments ₹594 cr (Mar-26) and ₹613 cr (Jun-26). We take 6.25% on ₹594 / 600 / 610 cr opening funds (capex roughly absorbs free cash flow): ₹37 / 37.5 / 38 cr. (2) Recurring non-treasury interest (loans ₹1.7 cr and other financial assets ₹1.9 cr, unchanged FY25-26): ₹3.6 cr, held at ₹4-5 cr. One-offs left out: asset-sale gain ₹1.2 cr, write-backs ₹0.5 cr, FX. FY27E ₹41 cr vs FY26 ₹43.8 cr and the twelve months to Jun-26 ₹36.5 cr (Screener).

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits reported under other financial assets, not in Screener's cash or investments: ₹104 cr non-current + ₹49 cr current at Mar-26 (AR notes 2.3a/b) less ₹7.8 cr earmarked for CSR and bank guarantees. With Screener's cash (₹34 cr) and mutual funds (₹404 cr) this gives the company's ₹583-594 cr.

assumptions._interestWhy: All finance cost is lease interest: ₹77.6 cr in FY26 on ₹764-891 cr of lease liabilities (~9%); ₹21.2 cr in Q1FY27 (₹85 cr annualised). New leases (~₹100-120 cr a year) add ~₹9-10 cr a year.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: there is no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT ₹84.0 cr, tax ₹21.4 cr (25.5%), attributable PAT ₹60.6 cr = 27.8% leakage (minorities ~2.3%). FY26 effective tax 21.4% included a one-off ₹13 cr deferred-tax credit at Rosewalk; underlying ~25.5%. Minorities: 24% of Prashanthi and Pratiksha (₹3 cr in FY26, ₹2 cr in Q1FY27); the Malad JV with doctors adds more from FY28.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend ~13-14% of profit since listing (₹3 a share paid in FY26, ₹30 cr); capex absorbs the rest.

dcf._betaWhy: No borrowings; lease liabilities are ~6% of enterprise value, so WACC (~11.0-11.1%) is close to the 11.3% cost of equity the engine uses. Defensive demand, but expansion risk outside the home markets.
dcf._tgWhy: Births are flat in India, but paediatric and maternity care is moving to organised, specialised hospitals and prices rise 5-6% a year: 6% nominal, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~20% to 9% by year 15: bed additions slow and the network matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 31% post-Ind AS (~26% pre-Ind AS): back near FY26 once the 2026-29 openings mature, but below FY24-25 (33%) as more beds sit in costlier markets (NCR, Mumbai).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. new leases falls from ~19-23% of revenue (expansion) to 11%: replacement of the asset base (depreciation ~8.5% of revenue) plus growth capex for 6-9% growth.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: A normal paediatric season returns, new hospitals reach 45%+ occupancy a year early, Mumbai and Gurugram open on time with high-acuity mix, and the margin recovers toward 32% (pre-Ind AS ~26.5%).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Two more weak seasons, occupancy stuck near 41-45%, the expansion outside the South (NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Indore) ramps slowly and burns cash, and the margin falls toward 28% (pre-Ind AS ~23%).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF (capex includes new leases), Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 6%, less net lease liabilities.

segments.note: Rainbow Children's Medicare (₹ crore). One reportable segment (medical and healthcare services; AR FY26 note 2.33), so there is no segment P&L. What the company does disclose: hospital KPIs every quarter (capacity and operational beds, occupancy, ARPOB, ALOS, IP discharges, OP consultations, deliveries, payor mix) for the network and for mature (>5 years) vs new hospitals; revenue split into hospital services, pharmacy and medical-service fee (annual). It does not disclose EBITDA by hospital group or by cluster. ANNUAL consRev = Screener consolidated sales; KPIs = company decks and AR. QUARTERLY consRev and consEbitdaMarginPct = Screener (post-Ind AS 116); KPIs = company decks, read from chart labels and checked against revenue (operational beds × days × occupancy × ARPOB). Quarters to Q1FY27 only (as of 30-Sep-2026). The mature/new split changed in Q1FY27 (Visakhapatnam and Hebbal moved to mature), so mature/new figures are shown only for Q1FY26, Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 on the new basis.

growth.text: Revenue compounded at 22.0% a year over 10 years (5y: 21.2%, 3y: 13.2%), from ₹234 cr to ₹1,703 cr.
Profit grew 32.2% a year over the same decade — faster than revenue, i.e. operating leverage.
Worst profit year: FY16 (-32.0%); best: FY22 (+245.0%).

margins.text: EBITDA margin has ranged 12.8%–34.1% since FY15 (peak FY23, trough FY16); FY26 was 32.2%.
Q1FY27 operating margin of 28.7% is lower than 86.4% of the 22 quarters on record — near the bottom of its history.
Raw-material cost moved from 12.86% to 13.33% of sales in FY26 (+0.47000000000000064 pts) — the single biggest swing factor in the cost base.

returns.text: ROE was 17.8% in FY26 (range 7.4–26.9% since FY15).
Stripping out cash and investments, return on operating capital was 18.9% vs headline ROCE of 17.0% — little distortion from the treasury book.
DuPont FY26: net margin 16.3% × asset turnover 0.7x × leverage 1.7x.

cash.text: Over 12 years the business generated ₹2,257 cr of operating cash flow (168.8% of reported profit), spent ₹1,489 cr on capex and paid ₹154 cr in dividends.
FY26 capex was 1.4x depreciation and 12.7% of sales — maintenance-level spending.
Cash conversion cycle of -73 days in FY26 — suppliers fund the working capital.

valuation.text: P/E of 48.7x vs since-listing (4.4-year) median 53.0x (range 31.3–121.3x); cheaper than 72.5% of that period (short history: treat with caution).
EV/EBITDA of 24.2x vs since-listing (4.4-year) median 26.1x (range 14.6–34.4x); cheaper than 68.6% of that period (short history: treat with caution).
P/B of 8.5x vs since-listing (4.4-year) median 9.8x (range 7.5–13.0x); cheaper than 78.4% of that period (short history: treat with caution).
At its since-listing (4.4-year) median P/E on current earnings, the stock would be ~₹1,430 vs ₹1,314 today (8.8%).

price.text: Stock down 2.9% over 1 year;  Currently 20.3% below its all-time high of ₹1,650.
Versus BSE-500: -2.9% vs -2.2% over 1 year; since 2022, 27.3% vs 12.1% a year.

ownership.text: Foreign institutions cut their stake from 22.3% to 16.0% over 11 quarters.
Domestic institutions raised their stake from 15.6% to 22.6% over 11 quarters.

Cash: maintenance ~₹45 cr a year; Gurugram ₹400-500 cr over two years (own land, own build); other projects at ₹65-70 lakh a bed (Coimbatore 130, Pune 150, Indore 100, Seegehalli 80, Malad fit-out); five-year plan ₹2,200 cr for 2,500 beds (~₹440 cr a year). FY26 capex ₹217 cr, Q1FY27 ₹56 cr. New leases are added because the model's net debt includes lease liabilities: right-of-use additions were ₹146 cr in FY26 (AR note 2.32), and Guntur, Malad, Indore and Seegehalli are leased. Engine workaround: a new lease adds an asset and a liability without cash, which the engine can only show as capex funded from net cash. The Nellore acquisition price is not disclosed and is left out.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹151 cr (incl. right-of-use depreciation ₹54 cr) = 6.6% of average gross block (₹2,294 cr); Q1FY27 ₹42 cr (₹169 cr annualised). 6.5% gives FY27E ≈ ₹181 cr with the new hospitals; the engine depreciates capex at once while projects sit in CWIP.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after lease liabilities, which is negative (₹583 cr of cash, deposits and investments less ₹891 cr of leases at Mar-26). Treasury income is built on gross cash in `otherIncome` instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 2.21). (1) Treasury income = yield × opening gross cash, deposits and mutual funds: FY26 ₹38.4 cr (bank interest ₹8.0 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹30.4 cr) on ~₹645 cr average funds = ~6.0%; company cash & investments ₹594 cr (Mar-26) and ₹613 cr (Jun-26). We take 6.25% on ₹594 / 600 / 610 cr opening funds (capex roughly absorbs free cash flow): ₹37 / 37.5 / 38 cr. (2) Recurring non-treasury interest (loans ₹1.7 cr and other financial assets ₹1.9 cr, unchanged FY25-26): ₹3.6 cr, held at ₹4-5 cr. One-offs left out: asset-sale gain ₹1.2 cr, write-backs ₹0.5 cr, FX. FY27E ₹41 cr vs FY26 ₹43.8 cr and the twelve months to Jun-26 ₹36.5 cr (Screener).

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits reported under other financial assets, not in Screener's cash or investments: ₹104 cr non-current + ₹49 cr current at Mar-26 (AR notes 2.3a/b) less ₹7.8 cr earmarked for CSR and bank guarantees. With Screener's cash (₹34 cr) and mutual funds (₹404 cr) this gives the company's ₹583-594 cr.

assumptions._interestWhy: All finance cost is lease interest: ₹77.6 cr in FY26 on ₹764-891 cr of lease liabilities (~9%); ₹21.2 cr in Q1FY27 (₹85 cr annualised). New leases (~₹100-120 cr a year) add ~₹9-10 cr a year.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: there is no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT ₹84.0 cr, tax ₹21.4 cr (25.5%), attributable PAT ₹60.6 cr = 27.8% leakage (minorities ~2.3%). FY26 effective tax 21.4% included a one-off ₹13 cr deferred-tax credit at Rosewalk; underlying ~25.5%. Minorities: 24% of Prashanthi and Pratiksha (₹3 cr in FY26, ₹2 cr in Q1FY27); the Malad JV with doctors adds more from FY28.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend ~13-14% of profit since listing (₹3 a share paid in FY26, ₹30 cr); capex absorbs the rest.

dcf._betaWhy: No borrowings; lease liabilities are ~6% of enterprise value, so WACC (~11.0-11.1%) is close to the 11.3% cost of equity the engine uses. Defensive demand, but expansion risk outside the home markets.
dcf._tgWhy: Births are flat in India, but paediatric and maternity care is moving to organised, specialised hospitals and prices rise 5-6% a year: 6% nominal, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~20% to 9% by year 15: bed additions slow and the network matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 31% post-Ind AS (~26% pre-Ind AS): back near FY26 once the 2026-29 openings mature, but below FY24-25 (33%) as more beds sit in costlier markets (NCR, Mumbai).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. new leases falls from ~19-23% of revenue (expansion) to 11%: replacement of the asset base (depreciation ~8.5% of revenue) plus growth capex for 6-9% growth.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: A normal paediatric season returns, new hospitals reach 45%+ occupancy a year early, Mumbai and Gurugram open on time with high-acuity mix, and the margin recovers toward 32% (pre-Ind AS ~26.5%).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Two more weak seasons, occupancy stuck near 41-45%, the expansion outside the South (NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Indore) ramps slowly and burns cash, and the margin falls toward 28% (pre-Ind AS ~23%).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF (capex includes new leases), Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 6%, less net lease liabilities.
